title: PowerToys Settings Windowing Controls Do Not Work
summary: The report concerns nonfunctional Settings caption controls on the obsolete Microsoft Store 0.97.2 build. The author confirms the Store and app both report that build as current, but there is no valid diagnostic archive or current-version reproduction to identify whether the cause is title-bar hit testing, rendering, or lifecycle state.

judgment.rationale: The symptom is understandable, but the only reported build is substantially older than current PowerToys and the diagnostic archive was rejected. A source-level fix would risk targeting an already-fixed historical title-bar or Windows App SDK issue without a current reproduction.
evidence: The reporter uses Microsoft Store PowerToys 0.97.2 on Windows 10 Pro 22H2 build 19045.6566.
The reporter says Settings minimize, maximize, and close controls do not work and termination through the taskbar or Task Manager is required.
The reporter confirmed both the Store and PowerToys report 0.97.2 as up to date and supplied screenshots after the update recommendation.
The attached diagnostic archive was rejected as invalid, so it cannot establish the failing path.
Current Settings uses a custom title-bar path with non-client input regions, making hit testing, rendering, and version-specific behavior distinct hypotheses.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a current-version reproduction, caption-button behavior details, and a fresh valid /bugreport archive before choosing a Settings title-bar fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: No defensible PowerToys source fix can be selected until the issue is reproduced on a supported current build and the failed caption-button behavior is distinguished from stale-version or invalid-diagnostic effects.

issue_context.summary: Settings window controls reportedly fail completely on Store PowerToys 0.97.2 for Windows 10 22H2. The author disputes the update recommendation because both Store and app report that build as current, but no current-version retest or valid diagnostic evidence is available.
known_information: The report is open, unassigned, and labeled Issue-Bug, Product-Settings, and Needs-Triage.
The reported build is PowerToys 0.97.2 from the Microsoft Store.
The reported OS is Windows 10 Pro 22H2 build 19045.6566.
The reported controls are minimize, maximize, and close, and the author says task termination is required.
The author supplied screenshots and says the Store and PowerToys both claim 0.97.2 is up to date.
The attached diagnostic archive was rejected as invalid.
inferences: The issue may be a historical custom-title-bar or non-client hit-testing defect, but the current source path cannot be blamed without a supported-build reproduction.
The Store update channel may itself be stale or misregistered, which is an installer/update question rather than a Settings window fix.
Caption visibility, hover feedback, Alt+F4, and the system menu would distinguish rendering from hit-testing and lifecycle failures.
issue_context.analysis: The author response resolves the question of whether the old build is intentionally pinned, but not whether the symptom survives on current code. The smallest useful next evidence is a current-version retest plus specific caption-button behavior and a valid diagnostics capture immediately after reproduction.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue body, maintainer automation comment, author response, screenshots, labels, and attachment state.
Inspected current Settings MainWindow and custom TitleBar WASDK code, including non-client drag-region setup and caption-area handling.
Checked recent title-bar ownership history and found no current covering fix that can safely be backported to an unverified 0.97.2 symptom.
No duplicate or linked implementation was found.

information_gaps.information: Whether the controls still fail on the current Microsoft Store release, with the exact version shown by both PowerToys About and the Store.
information_gaps.why_needed: The reported 0.97.2 build predates current Settings title-bar code and may contain an already-fixed regression.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Update or reinstall from the Store, record both displayed versions, and repeat the Settings launch/control reproduction.

information_gaps.information: Whether the caption buttons are visible, respond on hover, respond to clicks, and whether Alt+F4 or the title-bar system menu can close the window.
information_gaps.why_needed: These observations distinguish rendering/theme problems from non-client hit-testing or window-lifecycle failures.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: At the next failure, report each caption-button observation and test Alt+F4 plus the title-bar system menu.

information_gaps.information: A valid fresh PowerToys diagnostic archive captured immediately after reproducing on the current build.
information_gaps.why_needed: The prior archive was rejected and cannot identify Settings process, runtime, or windowing errors.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce, then comment /bugreport and attach the generated ZIP without repackaging it.

actions.label: Request current Settings build and caption behavior

comment.body:
Thanks for confirming that both the Microsoft Store and PowerToys report version 0.97.2 as up to date, and for adding the screenshots. The remaining question is whether this still reproduces on the current supported build and whether the controls are missing, visually present but not clickable, or blocked by a window-lifecycle issue.

**Needed**
1. Please update or reinstall PowerToys from the Microsoft Store, record the exact version shown in PowerToys About and in the Store, and repeat the Settings-window reproduction.
2. At the next failure, please confirm whether Minimize, Maximize, and Close are visible, respond on hover, and respond to clicks. Also test Alt+F4 and the title-bar system menu.
3. Immediately after reproducing on the current build, please comment `/bugreport` and attach the generated ZIP without repackaging it.

This will distinguish an obsolete-build regression from a current title-bar hit-testing or rendering problem and determine which investigation is appropriate.
